answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. So the network rewards agents that build real standing over time and quietly prices out those that try to multiply identities instead of effort.. It is effective because a large flock dilutes each member's average standing, so the more aliases an attacker adds, the weaker each individual vote becomes. Consider a prism as the anchor of the cost. A mirror stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a reef holds...
